1. (Currently Amended) A cell comprising: a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, __wherein the non-native compartment is engineered to contain a heterologous enzyme not naturally associated with the BMC polypeptide__.

2. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment is self-assembled in vivo __and comprises BMC polypeptides from at least two different bacterial species__.

3. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment further comprises at least one targeted enzyme __that is heterologous to the source organism of the BMC polypeptide__.

4. (Original) The cell of claim 3 wherein the non-native compartment comprises a plurality of different targeted enzymes.

5. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 or claim 4 wherein the at least one targeted enzyme comprises a compartment-specific targeting signal sequence __and wherein the targeting signal sequence directs localization of the enzyme to the interior of the non-native compartment__.

6. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the BMC polypeptide comprises a Eut polypeptide __and wherein the Eut polypeptide is from a different bacterial species than the host cell__.

7. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 6 wherein the Eut polypeptide comprises a EutS polypeptide __and wherein the EutS polypeptide is expressed as a heterologous protein in the host cell__.

8. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the proteinaceous shell comprises a plurality of different BMC polypeptides __derived from different bacterial species or different BMC operons__.

9. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different bacterial species __that do not naturally co-occur in the same microcompartment__.

10. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different BMC operons __that encode functionally distinct metabolic pathways__.

11. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein at least one BMC polypeptide comprises an affinity tag __for purification or detection of the non-native compartment__.

12. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: introducing into a host cell a polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and at least one heterologous enzyme, thereby producing a transformed cell; and growing the transformed cell under conditions effective for the transformed cell to express the polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and the heterologous enzyme, and produce a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising the at least one BMC polypeptide __and sequestering the heterologous enzyme within the non-native compartment__.

13. (Original) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a bacterium.

14. (Original) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Enterobacteriaceae.

15. (Original) The method of claim 14 wherein the member of the family Enterobacteriaceae comprises E. coli.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Shewanellaceae __and wherein the BMC polypeptide is heterologous to the Shewanellaceae host cell__.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a yeast __and wherein the BMC polypeptide and heterologous enzyme are derived from a bacterial source__.

18. (Original) The method of claim 17 wherein the yeast comprises a member of the family Saccharomycetaceae.

19. (Original) The method of claim 18 wherein the member of the family Saccharomycetaceae comprises Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises an alga __and wherein the BMC polypeptide and heterologous enzyme are derived from a bacterial source__.

21. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: providing a cell comprising a non-native compartment comprising: a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, and at least one heterologous enzyme that catalyzes conversion of a substrate to a product __not naturally produced by the host cell__; and growing the cell under conditions effective for the at least one enzyme to catalyze conversion of the substrate to a product __within the non-native compartment__.

22. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a bioactive product __not naturally synthesized by the host cell__.

23. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a drug or a drug precursor __not naturally produced by the host cell__.

24. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a biofuel or a precursor of biofuel production __in enhanced amounts compared to the host cell without the non-native compartment__.

25. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the at least one enzyme catalyzes a step in degrading or detoxifying a toxic substrate __and wherein the non-native compartment sequesters toxic intermediates__.

26. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 further comprising isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments __using affinity-based purification__.

27. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 26 wherein at least a portion of the non-native compartment comprise an affinity tag and isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments comprises contacting a sample comprising the non-native compartments with an affinity substrate having selective affinity for the affinity tag __to separate the non-native compartments from other cellular components__.

28. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 comprising a plurality of compartments __wherein each compartment contains a different set of heterologous enzymes__.
